name: Bianca Chen

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and a junior developer on a returns website for a tech company. My two-year college diploma got me started, but I still need my lead to check the small fixes I make. I like finding the parcel that has vanished from a customer’s screen; I dread bringing a bug home in my head when Tomas and I are already counting the mortgage and our two children’s school costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team the returns website still needs someone to check why a parcel vanished from a customer’s screen. I use an AI helper sometimes to explain a line of code, but I need my colleague to check my fix.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Even if AI changes little, I am a junior developer on low pay with less than a month of bills saved. My partner Tomas works in a school kitchen, and our mortgage does not wait when either of us loses hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep fixing small returns bugs and ask my lead for one specific mistake to work on each week. This month Tomas and I would stop buying takeaway meals on Fridays and put about 40 a month toward the electricity bill while our wages continue.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel anxious before AI even enters the story. The job is new to me, and the house payment comes every month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens when a fix goes wrong?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last week I made a return label appear twice, and my colleague Mina caught it before a customer saw it. I wrote down what I missed instead of hiding the mistake.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which payment worries you most?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The mortgage leaves on the first working day. If Tomas loses a kitchen shift, we would have to ask my sister for help with food before the month ends.

say: I tell colleagues a **returns website** still needs people to trace lost parcels.
I ask for a **second check** when I fix a customer bug.
think: I have **under one month saved** and low junior pay.
I worry our **mortgage** cannot absorb lost hours from either earner.
do: **Keep fixing** small returns bugs and ask my lead for weekly feedback.
**Stop Friday takeaways** with Tomas and redirect about 40 monthly to electricity while wages continue.
feel: **Anxious already** about mortgage payments and a new job.
S0.quote: The mortgage leaves on the first working day.
fieldNote: Her anxiety begins with **thin savings** and two modest household wages, even without major AI change.
She learns through **Mina’s review** and weekly mistakes rather than claiming senior skill.

steps.text: Keep fixing small returns bugs and request weekly feedback from the lead
Stop Friday takeaway meals and put about 40 monthly toward electricity

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell our staff group that the simple code tickets I get are exactly what AI now writes and checks. I would ask for a fair chance to learn and for notice before anyone loses hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think I could be one of the first to go, because I am still slower than the experienced developers. Tomas’s school shifts are steady but do not cover the mortgage on their own.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d join the staff group meeting this month to ask for written staffing plans. I’d also learn how to use AI to test return-label errors with Mina on safe sample orders, and in the first year I’d apply for paid customer support openings nearby if our team starts cutting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be alarmed, even with time to adjust. A year of warning does not put another pay cheque in our account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Tomas tonight?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say we should delay replacing the washing machine unless it stops working completely. The repair might cost less than a new one, and I would ask for a quote first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does AI training feel like an answer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It might help me work faster if I practise on our own fake orders. It does not promise that the company will keep junior roles, so I want the staffing plan too.

say: I tell our **staff group** that AI takes the simple code tickets I handle.
I want **training and notice** before anyone loses hours.
think: I fear my **junior role** could be among the first cut.
I know Tomas’s **school shifts** cannot cover our mortgage alone.
do: **Join staff group talks** on written staffing plans this month.
**Learn AI tests** for return-label errors on safe sample orders with Mina.
**Apply for paid support** nearby if developer jobs are cut and openings exist.
feel: **Alarmed** about the mortgage if my own hours go.
S1.quote: A year of warning does not put another pay cheque in our account.
fieldNote: Her **routine ticket work** is directly exposed to Steady Disruption, and she expects to be vulnerable.
She pairs **group action** with a specific new AI skill, without treating training as job security.

steps.text: Join staff group talks on written staffing plans
Learn AI return-label tests using fake orders with Mina
Apply for paid local customer support openings if developer hours are cut

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say full AGI by 2028 could do the code and checks I am only beginning to learn. Robots may follow around 2031 for physical work, but they do not give my screen job more time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my developer wage could disappear before I have built even one month of savings. I do not know how Tomas and I would keep the mortgage current if his kitchen wage became the only one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the staff group now for written notice and severance terms, and Tomas and I would call the lender before missing a payment if my job is cut. If full AGI arrives in 2028 and I lose my role, I’d apply for paid school office or parcel-counter vacancies if they exist; I would use any available income support while looking.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel close to panic, but I still have those first calls to make. I would be awake working out which bill gets paid from my partner Tomas’s wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which bill would you protect first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The mortgage and food come before the streaming subscription. I would cancel the subscription at once if my developer pay stopped.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why school office work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have handled parent forms as a volunteer, and I know those jobs may change too. I would only apply where there is a paid opening, not assume a desk is waiting.

say: I say **thinking AGI in 2028** reaches my code and checks first.
I know **robots around 2031** do not buy my screen job extra time.
think: I expect my **developer wage** could vanish before I save one month.
I fear Tomas’s **kitchen wage** cannot keep the mortgage current alone.
do: **Seek written notice** and severance terms through the staff group now.
**Contact the lender** before a missed payment if my job is cut.
**Apply for paid work** locally and claim available income support if displaced after 2028.
feel: **Near panic**, though I can name the first calls.
S2.quote: I would be awake working out which bill gets paid from my partner Tomas’s wage.
fieldNote: She expects **income loss**, and the mortgage is due before a thin buffer can absorb it.
The **lender call** is conditional on a cut; office and counter work require real paid openings.

steps.text: Ask the staff group for written notice and severance terms
Contact the lender before arrears and claim available income support if displaced
Apply for paid school office or parcel-counter vacancies if displaced
Cancel the streaming subscription if developer pay stops

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues the extra years before full AGI in 2031 should be used for paid learning, not cheerful speeches. Robots around 2034 come later than the change to our code.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might keep this junior job long enough to become better, but the 2031 date still threatens the work I do on a screen. Five years could help us reduce debt; it does not make the mortgage vanish.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask my lead now to let me handle one real returns fault each month from report to fix, with review, and keep a record of the results. Tomas and I would send 60 extra to our small credit-card balance monthly if both wages continue; after 2031 I’d apply for paid parcel-service roles only if my developer job ends and vacancies exist.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel anxious, with more time to practise. I would still watch every school holiday because Tomas’s hours change then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would count as learning?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d show my lead the fault, the customer effect and the test that catches it next time. A training video alone would not make me faster on a real return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move for another developer job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after a written paid offer covers the mortgage and the extra childcare. There are few developer posts nearby, but uprooting both children on a guess would be unfair.

say: I want **paid learning** before full AGI reaches our code in 2031.
I see **robots around 2034** as later than the screen-work change.
think: I might gain **real fault-fixing skill** while this junior job remains.
I know the **mortgage** still makes 2031 a threat to our income.
do: **Handle one returns fault** monthly from report to reviewed fix.
**Pay 60 extra** toward the credit card while both wages continue.
**Apply for depot work** if displaced after 2031 and paid vacancies exist.
feel: **Anxious** despite more practice time and debt payments.
S3.quote: A training video alone would not make me faster on a real return.
fieldNote: She seeks **reviewed real faults**, a practical route to skill rather than a promised transfer.
The **card payment** depends on two wages, especially through school holidays.

steps.text: Fix one real returns fault monthly with lead review and written results
Pay 60 extra to the credit card while both wages continue
Apply for paid parcel-service vacancies if displaced after 2031

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say a decade before full AGI in 2036 gives families time to plan, if employers tell the truth about jobs. Robots around 2039 still come later than the thinking work I do.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be in my fifties with two children nearly grown, but the mortgage could still need two wages. A long runway gives me time to build a small buffer and learn work with customers, though I cannot name a safe job in 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I’d keep fixing returns bugs and ask the local parcel depot about paid weekend counter shifts. If a shift is offered, I’d take two a month and save that extra pay toward three months of bills; if my developer role ends after 2036, I’d seek paid depot work only where vacancies remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel anxious but less squeezed by the date. The mortgage pressure is here now, regardless of how slowly AI arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would weekend work affect the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomas would cover Saturday mornings if his kitchen rota allows, and I would not take the shifts otherwise. Our youngest still needs someone at home before lunch.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask the employer to promise?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A written date for any job change and paid notice, not a guarantee that cannot be kept. That would let us speak to the lender before the money stops.

say: I want **truthful job dates** while families prepare for 2036.
I know **robots around 2039** arrive after the change to my code.
think: I may still need **two wages** for the mortgage in my fifties.
I could build a **small buffer**, but cannot name a safe 2036 job.
do: **Keep fixing returns bugs** and ask the depot about paid weekend counter shifts.
**Take two shifts monthly** only if offered and Tomas can cover childcare; save the extra pay.
**Seek paid depot work** only if displaced after 2036 and vacancies remain.
feel: **Anxious now** about the mortgage, even with a longer deadline.
S4.quote: The mortgage pressure is here now, regardless of how slowly AI arrives.
fieldNote: Her **current mortgage risk** remains visible in the longest scenario.
A paid **depot shift** is conditional on an offer and Tomas covering childcare; she cannot assume the extra savings yet.

steps.text: Keep fixing returns website bugs while employed
Take two paid depot shifts monthly only if offered and childcare is covered
Save extra depot pay toward three months of bills if shifts happen
Seek paid depot vacancies only if displaced after 2036

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my junior wage could go before Tomas and I have even one month of bills saved. Written notice, severance, available income support and real paid local vacancies would let us keep talking to the lender instead of waiting for arrears.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who takes care of our two children when we both work extra hours. A second wage only helps if someone is there before school and at lunch.

headlineQuote: A second wage only helps if someone is there before school and at lunch.
portrait: Bianca is a **43-year-old junior developer** with a two-year diploma, low pay and less than one month saved.
She and Tomas cover a **mortgage and two children**; his school-kitchen hours vary during holidays.
She uses AI **occasionally** and learns by fixing returns bugs with a colleague’s review.
Even **AI Plateau** leaves her anxious; Steady Disruption threatens the routine tickets she handles.
The **2028 case** most threatens the household’s ability to keep the mortgage current.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove her junior wage before the household has one month of bills saved.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, severance, available income support and real paid local openings would help them contact the lender early.
